*Settling in to think this through as the old farmer...*

Aiya, another year. My back don't bend like it used to, but the land still needs working. Let me think about what I'm doing this year, same as most years really.

I got 15 mu. About 10 mu I keep in wheat-maize like always — that's my food and my steady income. The other 5 mu I keep in cotton out west. My two sons work in town, but they come back to help at planting and at cotton picking time. My wife still cooks for everyone and helps in the field.

**Wheat (on 10 mu)** — Already planted back in October, so now I'm thinking about the spring work. When the wheat greens up after winter, I'll put down topdress fertilizer. I use urea, about one bag (50 jin, so 25 kg) covers maybe 2 mu for topdress. Before planting back in autumn I put down the compound fertilizer, maybe 2 bags per mu — that's what my father did, that's what I do. If the weather's dry at jointing I'll water it. Pumping water costs money though, electricity ain't free. Usually I water 2 times, maybe 3 if the sky don't help. Last year I got about 400 kg per mu, should be similar this year if no big wind knocks it down before harvest.

**Maize (on same 10 mu after wheat)** — Soon as wheat comes off in June, I got to get maize in fast. No time for deep plowing. I just use the small seeder my neighbor's son rents out, goes right into the stubble. Plant around June 15. I put some fertilizer with the seed, then topdress again when it's about knee-high. Maize don't need as much water as wheat — if it rains in July, August I don't need to pump at all. Good year gives me 450 kg per mu. Bad year, maybe 350. Can't really predict.

**Cotton (on 5 mu)** — Cotton is more work but the price been okay. Plant end of April when soil warms up. Saved some seed from last year, buy some new too. Cotton wants less fertilizer than grain but needs pesticide spraying — those bollworms are bad. My oldest son comes back to help spray, my knees can't handle carrying the pump. Picking time in September-October my wife and daughter-in-law help, sometimes hire one or two neighbor women by the day. Yield... maybe 250 kg lint per mu if it's a good year.

Money's always tight but we manage. I don't take credit, I pay cash for my inputs, that's how I've always done it. Don't need any fancy new varieties — what worked for 50 years will work now.
